goal_title: Book: L-Systems: Rules Grow Structure — improvements from the spine reading
why: The whole spine was read as a book on 2026-09-24, one sequence at a time, and every stumble, false claim or broken handover in lsystems became a task Palle can pick up one at a time. Reader: the VR visitor.
success_criteria: every open task here is done or skipped with a note
the chapters read through without a stumble in the headset
every code excerpt and number in the chapters matches the source

book.title: L-Systems: Rules Grow Structure
chapters_read: Fractal_Synthesis (last of fractals, for the handover in)
PG_Genetic_Evolution (first of proceduralgeneration, for the handover out)

reading.arc: The sequence takes one object out of the fractal halls, a sentence read by a turtle, and splits it into the two moments that were fused there: rewriting the sentence and reading it as movement. Each hall then adds one thing the bare grammar leaves out. Grammar Lab separates NEXT from TURN with HOLD as a witness; Growth follows the saved state through a bracket and lets length inherit; Grammars_And_Curves shows that even 'forward' is an assignment the reader makes; Architecture gives the line width, walls, rooms and a body that must fit; Competition gives the same rule a shared field and a turn order; Living goes behind the grammar to the raw gene and the counting threshold; Shape Grammars moves the rule from letters to faces and enlarges the result until the visitor stands beneath it; Assemblage closes on two marks and the paths a viewer reads into them. The question the sequence keeps asking, in nearly every closing paragraph, is what would have to be added before any of these drawings could hold, shelter, admit or obstruct a body. It is disciplined, checkable and unusually consistent in voice; its weaknesses are local (one desktop sentence, one unnamed button, two dangling callbacks, two missing attributions) rather than structural.
holds: The refrain 'these thin drawings have no collision surfaces / not yet somewhere to stand' closes Grammar Lab, Growth and Grammars_And_Curves, becomes the whole experiment in Architecture (a width and a body), returns as 'the floor stays solid' in Assemblage, and is picked up by Genetic Evolution's opening.
HOLD as a carried device: a witness copy of the current reading in Grammar Lab, Growth, Living and Assemblage; Living names it 'a witness', Assemblage cites Living for it, Genetic Evolution keeps it.

The bracket stack as the carried object: saved and restored state named at the end of Grammar Lab ('Carry the bracket into the next room'), enacted in Growth, re-read in Curves, given an address in Architecture, called 'the familiar brackets' in Competition, and found again inside Living's instrument.

The experimental form 'same X, different Y' at every desk: same sentence / different angle; same sentence / different reader; same grammar / different soil and turn order; same gene / different rounding; same samples / different marks.

Metres against fitting: Grammar Lab declares both drawings 'fitted to their display'; Growth and Curves put metre rulers beside unfitted readings; the distinction between what is drawn and what is measured runs to the 4x canopy in Shape Grammars and the 4x branch displays in Competition.
Every chapter ends by naming the next hall and the question it will carry, so the walk reads as one argument rather than eight exhibits.

hall_notes.note: Opens the sequence at one desk with two plinths and separates rewriting (NEXT) from interpretation (TURN), with HOLD as the witness; every count in it (five segments, 49 symbols / 25 instructions, four generations, 4,096 budget, 120 visible symbols) is checkable against grammar_lesson.gd and lsystem_editor.gd. Tight and well paced; it ends by handing the bracket to Growth.

Steps through F[+F]F[-F]F one symbol at a time in metres, making the stack and the inherited length (0.800 to 0.576) concrete, then turns length_decay above 1.0 into a small surprise (0.92 m branches, a 7.2 m trunk). The most instrument-like chapter and the one whose numbers are most carefully earned; its only slips are cosmetic.

Three readers of one sentence: reference, changed angle, and the x/y exchange. Its best move is reading the 'believing' turtle as a reflection across x = y that keeps lengths, angles and connectivity. Slightly abstract in the middle, and the reader is asked to verify a geometric claim by matching forks in the headset with no figure to check against.

The plan acquires width, walls, rooms and a boundary policy; the two-R / one-address trick and the 'leave the frame before you rebuild' rule are strong and both are real in the code. Contains the sequence's one desktop sentence, which is also wrong for the headset body, and the closing list of the rear collection omits a hatch and a vent that a visitor will meet.

A controlled pair on shared soil, with order, season and soil separated into buttons; the 2.250 / 1.980 uptakes reproduce exactly from the 5x5 sampling square and the one-cell offset in ForestCompetition.gd. Reads cleanly except that the button that takes a turn (STEP) is never named.

Goes behind the grammar to the raw gene and its rounding threshold (4.8 rounds to 2, 5.0 to 3), then HOLD and PLANT as witnesses that had to be written as copies. Conceptually the richest hall; weakened by one callback with no antecedent and a 'push to the upper limits' instruction that the compact desk makes laborious.

Two works and four served figures: the family of six cubes is patient and exact (0.4 m extrusion, 8% and 28% inset, twelve faces), and the canopy's 'Walk beneath it' is the sequence's one bodily reversal. Half again as long as any other chapter, and the closing paragraph spends itself on cross-references to Form Finding and Genetic Evolution rather than on the hall.

Closes on two marks and reader-made paths: ALPHABET holds the choices, ODDS holds the samples, STEP discards a row, and the floor pattern makes 'no collision boundary follows these lines' walkable. The coda on the loom and the galleries is generous and correctly attributed to Kristina Torsson, but the textile's own source, 10 PRINT, is never named although the exhibit label says it.

stumbles: LSystems_Competition: 'Let A take a turn' and 'Now let B take its turn' with no A or B button on the desk; the turn button is STEP and the chapter never names it.

LSystems_Architecture: 'The desktop body's collision capsule is sixty centimetres across' is spoken to a headset visitor whose body is forty centimetres across; the narrow passage is also forty centimetres, so the refusal the chapter promises is a desktop fact.
LSystems_Living: 'We have encountered this gap before. A trace records a hand at particular moments' has no earlier chapter behind it; the callback lands on nothing.
LSystems_Grammar_Lab: 'We have encountered an invisible point before' is a real callback to Point_One, the spine's first hall, thirteen sequences back, but it is unnamed.
LSystems_Growth: 'The pink point stays at the new tip' when the tip marker is pale cream in both views; pink is the held drawing.
Assemblage_Same_Desire: the original textile behind the desk is labelled '10 PRINT textile' and the chapter never says what 10 PRINT is.

LSystems_Architecture: the rear collection contains a floor hatch that opens as you approach and a vent that emits three walking bodies once a crystal is lifted; the closing paragraph lists only 'structure, dragon path, seed and mesh studies'.
LSystems_Grammars_And_Curves: 'reflects the entire construction across the diagonal x = y' must be verified by fork-matching in the hall; the chapter has no figure while Shape Grammars has four.

LSystems_Shape_Grammars: at 1220 words the chapter is 40 to 75 percent longer than every other; the canopy half re-explains extrusion and then leaves the hall for two cross-references before the handover.
LSystems_Grammar_Lab: 'Some segments may overlap' after TURN to 120 degrees; the five Koch segments at 120 degrees do not overlap, so the reader looks for something that is not there.

keep.quote: Our eyes receive a composed result: rewriting, interpretation, fitting, thickness, light. None is the untouched original behind the others.
F still means draw forward, but how far forward now depends on the state in which the turtle reads it.
The commitment is executable: F is assigned a direction through this code. We can change that assignment. We can also ask what the change has left untouched.
A plan can be legible to an eye long before it is usable by a body.
A body can remain visibly still while changing the conditions around it. To discover that here, we needed the field as well as the tree.
A control's appearance cannot tell us what kind of change it offers.
The form stays still; your movement changes what covers you.
The pleasure of finding a way through need not disappear when we learn how little the generator knew about it.

reading.handover_in: Clean. Fractal_Synthesis ends by sending the reader 'into the grammar laboratory' with the preset 'Koch Curve' that 'replaces F with F+F-F-F+F and turns ninety degrees' and the question 'What does an instruction become when another reader gives it a body?'. Grammar Lab opens on exactly that preset at generation zero (grammar_lesson.gd:34-36 sets preset 0, generations 0; lsystem_editor.gd:103 confirms the name, rule and 90 degrees), says 'We brought a construction out of the fractal halls', and asks 'Can one sentence have two bodies?'. The carried object (an explicit rule) and the carried question (a reader giving it a body) both arrive.
reading.handover_out: Works, with one wobble. Assemblage closes 'Next, generated forms will be compared using a numerical score... What changes when a program is asked to decide which result should continue?', and PG_Genetic_Evolution opens 'Six boxes wait beyond the desk... choose a body you would want to keep' and 'Here the program adds a judgement'. The next chapter's backward glance, however, reaches past Assemblage to Shape Grammars ('The cube family let us compare an altered amount with an altered face selection. We kept all six results'), which Shape Grammars had pre-announced ('Later, Genetic Evolution will let a score choose among described bodies'). The reader who has just left the textile hall is told they arrived from the cube hall; Assemblage's closing could carry one clause about the kept six results so the reference lands.
